title: Restaurant sparks outrage over $1 charge automatically added onto bill
text:
By BURNEY WONG - NEWS REPORTER

Published:  16:03 AEST, 31 August 2026   |  Updated:  16:03 AEST, 31 August 2026

86

View  comments

An outraged diner has slammed a hospitality group after discovering a $1 charity fee had been automatically added to their bill.

Lucas Collective owns 15 venues including Maison Batard and Chin Chin, and adds the gold coin donation to bills unless diners ask staff to remove it when paying.

The donation goes to Collective Foundation, a charity set up by Lucas Collective founder Chris Lucas.

The practice became public after a customer posted a photo of his Maison Batard receipt on Reddit.

'A $1 charitable donation has been added to your bill in support of Collective Foundation,' it read.

'This can be removed from your bill at your request. Please let our team know.'

It also explained how the donation would help the charity.

'Collective Foundation is a registered charity dedicated to the long-term future of hospitality,' it read.

A hospitality group has been slammed over a $1 charity fee at its restaurants, with customers required to notify staff to opt out

'Funds raised support the design and delivery of industry leadership programs to support professional development across the sector.'

According to the Collective Foundation website, the funds also help with industry research.

'The Foundation is also undertaking research to better understand career progression and the opportunities and challenges facing people working across Australia's hospitality sector,' it said.

'Through the support of our hospitality community, the Foundation is working to create lasting benefits for the industry and the people who make it what it is.'

The Foundation reiterated that $1 donations across Lucas Collective venues are optional.

'Participation is entirely voluntary, so if you would prefer not to contribute, simply let your waitperson know and the contribution will be removed from your bill,' it said.

The customer said he received 'no prior notice' of the extra dollar and asked staff to remove the charge 'out of principle'.

Many Aussies were outraged by the scheme.

Lucas Collective owns and operates 15 venues, including Maison Batard and Chin Chin, and adds the gold coin donation to bills unless diners tell staff they wish to decline when paying

The donation goes towards Collective Foundation, a charity established by Lucas Collective founder Chris Lucas

'The government needs to get in now and ban this practice. These sorts of things need to be opt-in, not opt-out,' one said.

'I am happy to support charities, but I am choosing which ones I donate my money to,' another added.

'Automatically adding it to my bill will guarantee that I will not support it and I will not be a return customer.'

Others were shocked that Lucas Collective was collecting donations for a charity founded by its own owner.

'If the restaurateur wants to donate "per-bill", they can, but making your customers do it for you is not ok,' one said.

Daily Mail contacted Lucas Collective and Collective Foundation for comment.
